items.note: DETECTOR CAUTION on this source. The Maersk routing API exposes a boolean isRoutingAdhoc. On CNYTN-USHOU it is true only for this XL row and false for all eight TP15 rows, which looks like a clean ad-hoc label. On KRPUS-USHOU it is true for EVERY row including all eight TP15 proforma sailings. It therefore behaves like a per-pair routing attribute, not an ad-hoc marker, and must be treated as context only - the same way isGemini is - never as a trigger. This voyage stays classified as an extra loader on the strength of the serviceName XL / serviceCode 770 being absent from every alliance registry, not on that flag. vsProforma uses the modal TP15 transit observed this run (33 days across 4 of 8 sailings); the 17 Sep record used 34, so the 1-day move in deltaDays is a proforma-side change, not a slip.

New trap for the Maersk source, same shape as the Hapag isGemini trap. The routing-unified response carries isRoutingAdhoc. On CNYTN-USHOU it is true only for the XL row and false for all eight TP15 rows. On KRPUS-USHOU it is true for all nine rows including every TP15 proforma sailing. It is a per-pair routing attribute, not an ad-hoc label. Never trigger on it. If a future run flags eight TP15 sailings as extra loaders, this is why.

Evergreen coverage this run is 4 weeks, not 8. TVS2 durationWeek accepts a maximum of 28 days and the second pass at departureDay plus 28 was not run. Evergreen sightings therefore cover roughly ISO weeks 39 to 42 only; weeks 43 to 46 are unscanned on that carrier. A new OGEC voyage departing in November would not appear in this file.
